title: Traffic-steering config spec and gating runbook
body:
Purpose:
This note defines the canonical traffic-steering configuration schema we use in the control plane, the validation layers that must run before a config is accepted, and the rollout mechanics (automatic and manual) for progressive deployment across regions and capacity tiers. Goal is to minimize surprises during model or variant transitions and to make gating reproducible and auditable.

Scope and principles:
- Declarative small-surface config: single YAML blob per logical route.
- Validation-first: syntactic checks, semantic checks (model compatibility, region availability), and dry-run capacity checks before any rollout.
- Progressive traffic slices with automated metric gates and human approvals for non-trivial changes.
- Fail-fast rollback with telemetry-driven triggers and an explicit runbook for SREs.
- Configs are authored in PRs against infra-config repo; CI validates and endorses.

High-level fields (intention):
- route_id: logical name for the application route (string)
- selector: identity of requests this route applies to (prefix, header, customer_id)
- target_clusters: ordered list of candidate model variants or backends with weights and health policy
- fallback: fallback strategy when preferred targets fail (region fallback, model-fallback)
- rollout: declarative rollout plan (phases: canary -> ramp -> full)
- constraints: region constraints, capacity limits, license/security flags
- metadata: author, changelist id, link to PR/Jira

Minimal example YAML (authoritative example for PRs):

---
route_id: in-app-summarize-v2
selector:
  header: "x-product-route: summarize"
  prefix: "/api/v1/summarize"
target_clusters:
  - id: model-gamma-quantized
    weight: 10
    region_constraint: [us-west1, us-east1]
    min_available_capacity: 4
    compatibility_tags: [decoder-only, kvcache-v1]
  - id: model-gamma-fp16
    weight: 90
    region_constraint: [us-east1]
    min_available_capacity: 8
    compatibility_tags: [decoder-only, kvcache-v1]
fallback:
  type: model_variant
  prefer: model-gamma-quantized
  fallback_region: us-west1
rollout:
  strategy: progressive
  phases:
    - name: canary
      percent: 5
      duration: 30m
      checks:
        - latency_p95: < 750ms
        - error_rate: < 0.5%
        - cost_per_token: <= 1.2x baseline
    - name: ramp
      percent: 50
      duration: 1h
      checks:
        - latency_p95: < 800ms
        - error_rate: < 1.0%
    - name: full
      percent: 100
      duration: 0
constraints:
  regions: [us-east1, us-west1]
  must_support_kv_cache: true
metadata:
  author: maya.patel@redwood.ai
  pr: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4321
---

Validation tiers (CI + control plane):
1) Linting (pre-commit / CI)
   - YAML schema lint (required fields, types, field names).
   - No hard-coded capacity IDs or hostnames in config; use cluster ids.
   - Ensure metadata.pr points to an existing PR or ticket format.
2) Semantic checks (CI-run integration tests / control-plane dry-run)
   - Model compatibility: requested compatibility_tags must be satisfied by model metadata in model-catalog.
   - Region availability: target clusters must advertise sufficient capacity in requested regions. Dry-run queries capacity planner.
   - Security flags: if config enables private-only access or KMS, verify team has entitlement.
3) Policy checks (policy-engine)
   - Ensure rollout.percent steps do not exceed org caps for automatic ramping (e.g., no >10% canary without manual approval for enterprise customers).
   - Enforce blackout windows (no big rollouts during deploy freeze).
4) Pre-flight cost estimate (optional but recommended)
   - Control plane computes expected delta in token cost and surface as comment on PR.

CI gate commands (examples the infra repo CI will run):
- tools/config-lint --schema=traffic-steering-v2.yaml path/to/config.yaml
- tools/semantic-validate --dry-run --route route_id
- ./scripts/preflight-cost-estimate.sh path/to/config.yaml --output comment
- GH action posts checklist and required approvals

Automated rollout mechanics (control-plane behavior):
- When a config is merged to main and passes CI, an automated job enqueues the rollout.
- For strategy: progressive, the control-plane will start the first phase and create a short-lived canary slice.
- During each phase, the control-plane continuously samples metrics for the route and compares to baseline or configured checks. Baseline is prior-route's 30m rolling window immediately before phase start.
- If checks pass for the configured duration, shift to next phase; otherwise trigger automated rollback to last stable config.
- The control-plane creates structured events for each phase transition (phase_started, phase_success, phase_failed) and posts to the route audit log.

Metric checks (authoritative list):
- latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99 (ms)
- user_facing_error_rate (5xx and 4xx mapped by request type)
- classifier_fallback_rate (how often tool-calling/fallback happened)
- token_throughput (tokens/sec on the serving cluster)
- cost_per_token (estimated)
- quality_guardrails: BLEU-like or eval prompt set regression rates if available

Gate/threshold semantics:
- A check defined as "latency_p95: < 800ms" means the observed p95 over the phase window must be strictly less than 800ms.
- Operators can specify relative checks: "latency_p95: <= 1.15x baseline"; control plane resolves this to an absolute threshold.
- Failure tolerance: multiple transient breaches are smoothed with a configurable "breach_count" and "breach_window" to avoid noisy rollbacks. Default: breach_count=3 within breach_window=2m triggers phase fail.

Manual approval and exception flows:
- If a rollout plan contains a phase with percent > 10% and target includes enterprise-customer routes, require manual approval (GH reviewers group: platform-release).
- For emergency rollouts flagged by a blocker ticket, there is an "override" flag but it must be accompanied by a post-rollout audit (who allowed it, why) and is gated by SRE pager duty.

Rollback playbook (quick steps for on-call SRE):
1) Identify failing route and phase in control-plane UI or via /api/v1/rollouts/{id}/status.
2) If automated rollback already initiated, follow audit: check reason, time, impacted regions.
3) To manually rollback: POST /api/v1/routes/{route_id}/rollback with body: { to_revision: <stable-revision-id> } (the API requires an SSO token and a 2-approver confirmation for >30% rollback).
4) If rollback fails due to capacity (cannot route to fallback clusters), follow escalation: add temporary capacity via "capacity-ops" runbook or open infra incident.
5) After rollback, run post-mortem: capture metric diffs, list of failed checks, related PRs and commits.

Testing and staging hygiene:
- All authors must test route config in the staging control-plane using a full dry-run. A dry-run will validate model catalog compatibility and produce a simulation report.
- Use synthetic traffic (from load-generator job) to exercise KV cache and batching behavior for the new target cluster.
- Maintain a small set of canonical prompt tests for each route (prompt set runners) to validate quality regressions at canary stage.

Observability and audit needs:
- Every rollout should produce an immutable timeline with events: author, PR, CI checks, phase events, metric deltas, approvals, and final outcome.
- Route audit logs must be retained for 1 year by default for compliance.
- Integrate with slack notifications for phase failures and final status.

Open questions / next steps:
- How to standardize quality-guardrails across different product teams (common metrics and prompt sets)?
- Should we support weight-expressions for gradual traffic shifting (instead of discrete percent steps)?
- Add an automated cost-sensitivity gate that optionally prevents ramp if cost delta > X% for low-margin routes.

Appendix: quick checklist for PR reviewers
- [ ] Schema lint passes with tools/config-lint
- [ ] Semantic validation OK (model tags, regions, capacity preflight)
- [ ] Rollout phases present and have sensible durations/percents
- [ ] Metadata links to PR/ticket and author contact
- [ ] If automatic gate needed, confirm policy exemptions or manual approval steps included
- [ ] Add post-deploy verification prompts and prompt-set names to metadata

This doc is a working runbook — comments welcome. If you are authoring a config, start from the YAML example above and run the CI locally.
